problem: Prior EQA agents either ground VLM planners in images only (Explore-EQA's 2D semantic map, huge image memories) or use offline-built semantic scene graphs; no memory is simultaneously online, compact and semantically rich, so VLMs are poorly grounded in the current environment, use many planning steps and are overconfident.
motivation: EQA needs both commonsense priors (where things usually are) and grounding in the actual scene (where the agent is and has been). Real-time 3D scene graphs are compact but have only closed-set, task-agnostic semantics, while images are rich but bulky, so combining them could give efficient, grounded planning without offline processing.
key_idea: Ground a VLM planner in a real-time hierarchical 3D metric-semantic scene graph (Hydra) enriched with room labels and semantic frontiers, plus a small SigLIP-selected task-relevant image memory, and plan hierarchically (room -> region -> object, or frontier) until it is confident.
insight: The multimodal memory is what matters: the SG-only ablation collapses to 13.6% SR and the vision-only ablation with random frontiers reaches 45.7% (overconfident, 1.0 steps), versus 63.5% for the full method. The incrementally built compact graph even beats SayPlanVision with the full offline scene graph (63.5 vs 54.8 on HM-EQA), suggesting large contexts hurt VLM inference and cause overconfidence. Error analysis shows fewer false positives (6.36% vs 24.56% for Explore-EQA-GPT4o), meaning the grounding stops the VLM from guessing by commonsense.
method: Online 3DSG construction: Hydra builds layered graph (mesh, objects, regions/places, rooms, building) from RGB-D, poses and semantic segmentation (GT HM3D semantics in sim, Detic in real world), plus a 2D occupancy map from TSDF.
Room enrichment: an LLM is prompted with the list of objects in each room node to assign semantic room labels (e.g. kitchen) replacing generic R0, R1.
Frontier enrichment: frontiers from the 2D occupancy map are clustered and added as graph nodes, each linked to its top-3 nearest objects within 2 m, so the VLM can choose frontiers semantically.
Task-relevant visual memory: images sampled during execution are scored with SigLIP against question keywords; top K=2 are kept and concatenated with the current view as VLM input.

Hierarchical VLM planner: takes question, choices, serialized scene graph, images, history and state; outputs answer, boolean and numeric confidence, reasoning, and action Goto_Object_node (choosing room, region, then object) or Goto_Frontier_node (justified by connected objects); uses structured output enums.
Confidence-based termination: stop when confident=True or confidence >0.9, or at T_max; the prompt tells the VLM the scene graph is imperfect and to seek visual confirmation.
Navigation execution: shortest path on the obstacle-free 2D occupancy map, camera oriented toward the target node during motion.

setting.backbone: GPT-4o, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Llama 4 Maverick (frozen VLM planners, prompted); SigLIP for image relevance; Hydra for scene graph
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D images with camera poses/intrinsics; semantic segmentation (GT in sim, Detic in real world)
setting.action_space: high-level Goto_Object_node / Goto_Frontier_node executed via shortest-path waypoints on a 2D occupancy map
setting.simulator: Habitat-Sim (HM3D-Semantics scenes) plus real-world Hello Robot Stretch RE2
setting.privileged: GT semantic segmentation masks from HM3D-Semantics in simulation (Detic used in real world)

numbers.extra: multiple-choice, confidence-based termination; GT semantic segmentation; success = correct and confident
numbers.evidence: Table 1 (comparison to simulation baselines), HM-EQA columns

numbers.eval_set_note: 113 A-EQA questions in HM3D scenes only, augmented with LLM-generated multiple-choice answers

numbers_note: SR is the success rate defined as correct and confident answer; 'Steps' and 'TL' are avg planning steps and trajectory length (m) over successful episodes, not standard benchmark metrics. HM-EQA split labeled 'test' since the paper does not name a split.
results: GraphEQA-Gemini-2.5Pro reaches 67.0% SR on HM-EQA and GraphEQA-GPT4o 63.5% (vs 51.7% Explore-EQA, 54.3% best Explore-EQA variant, 54.8% SayPlanVision), with far fewer planning steps (about 2-5 vs 18.7). On OpenEQA A-EQA (HM3D subset, multiple-choice) GPT-4o reaches 69.1% vs 55.3% for Explore-EQA; in the open-vocabulary setting 53.6% vs 41.8% Multi-Frame VLM (as reported in the OpenEQA paper).
limitations: Depends on off-the-shelf segmentation/detection, so scene graph semantics are closed-set and limited to detected categories (GT segmentation used in simulation).
VLM planners can be over- or under-confident, causing premature or late termination.
Limited to single-floor scenes; the real-world evaluation is small (about 15 trials in two homes plus qualitative office/workshop).
